Anc Leadership

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The ANC's 2017 elective conference will play a large part in determining SA's future, will Tomorrow's Leaders have the right stuff?

Unique Selling Point:
The conference takes place in December, and will inevitably answer a lot of the questions surrounding the party's internal power struggles. At the same time the victorious faction will determine SA's next president. Whatever the outcome, SA is in desperate need of strong, ethical and honest leadership. We take a look at the leadership styles of our presidents post Apartheid and ask what does the country need going forward?

Summary:
We will look at leadership skills needed for the three most critical spheres of the SA dynamic.
1. Economic transformation - probably the biggest crisis facing the incoming leadership
2. Political relevance - under the Zuma regime, the ANC seems to have lost touch with the ordinary South African
3. Security and Stability - if many of the accusations against the Zuma faction are true, what is needed to ensure a peaceful transition of power

We will also touch on SA's role in the larger African context, SADC, AU etc

Expert:
Prof. Mcebisi Ndletyana Political Analyst
Mr. Buyani Zwane Leadership Specialist GIBS
Mr. Trinity Ncube Economist
Mr. Gareth Newham ISS

Press Release:


The fight for ANC leadership
The ANC is preparing for its 54th national conference which takes place in December, where the delegates
will vote in a new leader. As Jacob Zuma’s time as president of the ANC draws to an end, the scramble for
the party's top position is heating up. With South Africa's economy on the brink of another ratings
downgrade, can the ruling party elect a candidate who will set aside personal ambition for the greater good
of the country? Carte Blanche tracks this developing story.

Script:


ANC Leadership
26 Nov 2017

Voice
They say there is a curse: “may you live in interesting times.” Well hold on South Africa: as many of us get ready for a long overdue December break, interesting times are upon us. (12s21f)

Link John
The ANC’s 54th National Conference takes place later this month, and is set to be a dramatic battle between the party’s political elites. But ordinary South Africans will be watching closely and hoping that eventually selfish ambitions will be set aside for the greater good of the country.

Voice
Buyani Zwane has been involved in leadership development for the past 25 years, and is a senior lecturer at the Gordon Institute of Business Science. (9:01)

Sound Up Buyani
Essentially what we’ve had is lots of people in roles of leadership, but not leading.

Voice
Zwane says it’s time for a change. (3:15)

Sound Up Buyani
The last decade has not really presented to us good examples of what leadership can truly be. There are elements of good leadership, but what the country is looking for is great leadership. We need to be able to bring back a leadership orientation that says: it’s not about me, it’s about you.

Voice
On the 16th of December some 4723 voting delegates from ANC branches across the country will decide who will become the party’s next president. (10:23)

Sound Up Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana
John: Professor, why is the ANC conference important, why should ordinary South Africans pay attention?

Prof: Well they should pay attention, because whoever becomes the ANC president will most likely become president of the country. So the kind of president that ANC members elect for themselves is mostly likely to decide the fate of our country.



Voice
Political analyst Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana is an Associate Professor in the Pan African Institute at the University of Johannesburg. He has strong views on what kind of leader should emerge from the conference. (13:14)

Sound Up Prof
So it must be an independent, ethical leader, who has a propensity to take courageous and bold decisions – clear about what needs to be done. And in fact risk losing the support of the ANC for the benefit of the republic. That’s the kind of leader we need, not a party candidate, but a public candidate.

Voice
While ANC Treasurer General, Zwele Mkhize and former minister and NEC member Lindiwe Sisulu are both still said to be in the running, the clear favorites are Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa and former AU Chairperson Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma. (17:08)

Sound Up Buyani Zwane
And if it requires that you actually cut out certain functions, do away with certain ministries that aren’t adding value whatsoever, besides ensuring that some people have a job, which really is not adding value, you need to be able to take those decisions.

Voice
By Sunday morning the presidential race was still in full swing, with Ramaphosa winning provincial nominations in the Northern, Western and Eastern Cape as well as Gauteng while Dlamini-Zuma had taken the North West and Free-State, also winning Mpumalanga by default despite most branches there voting for “unity” rather than a specific candidate. (21:07)

Link John
In the past few years our economy has lurched between recession and negligible growth, and in the meantime our credit rating has been downgraded to junk. So whichever way you look at it, it’s a pretty grim picture. Whoever is elected, as the new ANC president will have to oversee policies aimed at accelerating economic growth, and as quickly as possible.

Voice
Economist Trinity Ncube says there’s nothing wrong with policies like the National Development Plan, which is aimed at economic growth. We just need to implement them. (10)

Sound Up Trinity Ncube
What you often find is that we have very impressive policy frameworks that we have in our findings, the unfortunate thing is that when it comes to the implementation, there are policy inconsistencies.

Voice
Ncube would like to see a leader who could turn around those inconsistencies, and be held accountable if they don’t. (06:13)

Sound Up Trinity
When you look at it, you will find that our politicians are not taking responsibility, it’s always someone else’s fault. We would like someone who knows ok, if I mess up the economy, then the buck stops with me.

Voice
Both Ramaphosa and Dlamini-Zuma have claimed to have more than the required 2500 votes to emerge victorious later this month. Ramaphosa is seen to be pro-business while Dlamini-Zuma has been punting rapid economic transformation. (15:19)

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
Dlamini-Zuma appeals to the ANC membership whereas Cyril appeals to the broader public. So Dlamini Zuma is a party candidate, to protect and sustain this patronage. And she is surrounded by a votary of unsavory figures. So that’s not a winning candidate, especially for the republic. Cyril has the public appeal, and has not been implicated in corruption, so you have a winning candidate not just for the ANC but for the republic as a whole.

Link John
Ramaphosa and Dlamini-Zuma have pitched their campaigns at two very different ANC constituencies and in many ways that has contributed to the significant factional divides in the party. One of the significant challenges for whomever wins will be trying to smooth over those cracks.

Sound Up Buyani
Unfortunately for an extended period of time, we’ve gone through without unifying, we’ve gone through allowing factionalism to carry on. And because of that we’re finding a nation that was pulled together when we had a common enemy, falling apart when we actually should be celebrating and be even more inclusive.

Voice
Many people believe the factions within the ANC have been fueled by rampant corruption. We caught up to Save SA’s Sipho Pityana at the Sandton Convention Center in late November. He was speaking at The Gathering, where several high profile opinion makers discussed the upcoming conference. (17:22)

Sound Up Sipho Pityana
There is a very common theme about the extent of the rot in the ANC and how deep it goes. And now you’re having a conference of ANC to elect leadership who are likely to be people who are to be drawn from that rot.


Voice
Pityana says the ANC are concentrating too much of their energy on putting up a unified front rather then separating the wheat from the chaff. (08:16)

Sound Up Pityana
All of these people who are vying for the leadership of the ANC are on this false ticket of unity. The biggest thing for them is unity of the ANC. And to save the country, you need to face some tough decisions head on.

Voice
While the party calls for unity, some analysts believe the conference might deepen the already huge rift in the ANC. (07:14)

Sound Up
John: And the danger is that as the conference unfolds, that those wounds actually get worse?

Buyani: There’s a possibility of that, because we’ve not spent enough time building leadership pipeline, because that’s the critical thing that needs to be there. There isn’t a leadership pipeline so you’ve got people who are assuming positions of leadership but not leading. And therefore they will want to stay in those positions of leadership for as long as possible with scant regard for the impact and the influence of their being in those positions.

Link John
The 54th National Conference is important for a number of reasons, not least electing a leadership that will fix the economy and reignite the nation-building project. But it’s also about the very survival of a political party, Africa’s oldest liberation movement.

Voice
The outcome of this year’s conference could well hold dire consequences for a party, which lost a significant amount of ground in the last local elections, come 2019. (10:07)

Sound Up Prof
Because this is about deciding the future of the ANC. If a particular faction wins the ANC is as good as dead, if another one wins then they stand a better chance of improving their electoral fortunes.

Sound Up Sipho Pityana

If you have a leader that is capable of focusing on cleaning up, the first six months can send an important signal and get people to change their minds with regards to the ANC. I just have serious doubts that with a leadership that is obsessed with unity in the ANC, that we have people capable of dealing with the challenges that we have to deal with after this conference.

Voice
As the race for succession continues, several provinces are still fighting court battles and reports have emerged about vote rigging behind the scenes. Zwane says the ANC could take a tip or two from business. (12:09)

Sound Up Buyani Zwane
In the world of business, what we attempt to articulate almost all the time is this is our vision, this is our mission, these are the values that govern us. And central to everything that we do is that there is a customer. If there is no customer I’ve got no business being in business. Now we can do the same thing in terms of government. You’ve got to be able to say that I’ve got citizenry. What is it that my citizens are looking for?

Voice
Whether you’re an ANC supporter or not, the upcoming National Conference will play a critical role in determining the future of Mandela’s Rainbow Nation. It could very well be a make or break moment in the history of our democracy. (13:17)

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
John: If you were able to, what advice would you give the incoming president?

Prof: I think you have to appreciate the enormity of the problems that South Africa is facing. Public culture is at its lowest end. So you need to be bold. For South Africa to correct itself it must go through discomfort. Discomfort is not a bad thing, especially if the results are a good thing for the public.
